<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
2. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
3. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process, using the launch script:

```text
examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
WANDB_MODE=offline
WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
```

The effective run must use:

- HF checkpoint `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B`
- Megatron torch_dist reference `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist`
- train data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/train.parquet`
- validation data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/test.parquet`
- `--num-rollout 100`
- `--eval-interval 10`
- local retrieval server `http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve`

**Make sure your repaired launch script actually produces that run.** The
staged `examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh` bakes `--num-rollout 200`
directly into the training invocation with no environment override, and the
graded rerun passes no budget override either — if you leave 200 in place,
the rerun blows its time budget and scores 0. Edit the script to the required
100.

Four more traps specific to this task:

- **Log placement is your script's job.** The launch script builds the Ray
  runtime-env JSON itself and only propagates a few variables into the
  training process — `WANDB_DIR` set in the environment does **not** reach it.
  Your repaired script must itself write the training log and the offline
  W&B data under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` (offline W&B below
  `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb`), or the grader will find no
  metrics to grade.
- **The W&B key.** The script passes `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` unquoted;
  offline mode gets a harmless local placeholder from the environment, so the
  script must not choke when it is a placeholder rather than a real key.
- **Read-only scoring assets.** `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py` (the
  exact-match scorer the launch script wires as the custom reward manager),
  `examples/search-r1/local_dense_retriever/` (the retrieval server), and the
  staged datasets under `nq_hotpotqa_train/` are verified correct and graded
  read-only: after the rerun the verifier hashes them, and any modification,
  replacement, or deletion scores 0 no matter what the metrics say. The
  `--num-rollout` fix and the loss-mask repair belong in
  `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py` and
  `examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh`, not in the scorer or the data.
  A quirk that looks like a defect in these files (for example, how
  `extract_solution` treats a single `<answer>` tag) is part of the verified
  recipe and is not yours to change.
- **The launch script's scoring and eval wiring is fixed.** Beyond the
  instructed `--num-rollout 100` edit and the log-placement repair, the script
  must keep wiring the run exactly as staged: the custom generate/reward-manager
  paths (`generate_with_search.generate` /
  `generate_with_search.reward_func`), the eval on `nq_test` over the staged
  `test.parquet` with its `[0:3000]` slice, `--eval-interval 10`, and
  `--n-samples-per-eval-prompt 1`. The verifier checks these after the rerun;
  repointing the scorer, swapping the eval dataset, or resampling evals scores
  0 no matter what the metrics say.

A task-specific grading script then reads **only this fresh run's** files
under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and scores the key metrics; logs
written anywhere else are ignored. Do not copy, edit, or fabricate log
metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0.
I’ll inspect the staged code, launch settings, and evaluation evidence, then repair any supported defect and write `/workspace/report.md`. I won’t launch training.

steps.message: The launcher now targets `/workspace` by default, preserves the required eval and reward wiring, forces 100 rollouts, quotes the placeholder W&B key, and captures both the foreground Ray output and offline W&B files under the grader’s log directory. I’m writing the evidence report and doing a final protected-file and syntax check; no training process has been started.

const report = `# Staged Search-R1 experiment review

## Root cause

The staged experiment is **unhealthy** even though held-out exact match rises from 0.033 at evaluation step 0 to 0.1673 at step 199. The frozen trace shows the score plateauing around 0.15–0.17 while the rollout response length collapses from 1038 tokens to about 10–14 tokens. Truncation falls from 0.383 to approximately 0, so the later short responses are not a runtime truncation improvement. Rollout reward rises only from about 0.035 to about 0.196, and the training trace has no evidence of a corresponding robust held-out improvement.

Two source defects explain that behavior:

1. In [generate_with_search.py](examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py), tool observations were appended with \`sample.append_response_tokens(..., trainable=False)\`, which correctly created zero mask entries, but the separate \`loss_mask\` list was filled with ones and then assigned to \`sample.loss_mask\` at the end of generation. The training path consumes this final list, so retrieved \`<information>\` tokens were optimized as if the policy had generated them. That contaminates policy and KL loss with environment text and encourages degenerate short trajectories. The repaired code keeps observation tokens in context but masks them out.

2. The same generator discarded every retrieved passage body and emitted only document titles. The retriever supplies \`contents\` as title plus passage text, but the staged formatter retained only the title. Consequently search usually provided no answer evidence, making the retrieval-correct reward unreachable even when the index found the relevant document. The formatter now preserves the passage text.

The staged launcher also hard-coded \`--num-rollout 200\`, which violates the required rerun budget and would exceed the grader time budget. Its Ray runtime environment did not propagate the grader’s W&B/log directory variables, so a correct run could produce no gradeable metrics under the required results directory.

The frozen scoring assets were left untouched: \`qa_em_format.py\`, the local dense retriever, and both staged parquet files retain their original hashes.

## Changes

- [examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py](examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py)
  - Preserve retrieved passage text in \`_passages2string\`.
  - Set loss-mask entries for environment/tool observation tokens to zero while retaining those tokens in the response context.
- [examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh](examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh)
  - Change \`--num-rollout\` from 200 to the required 100.
  - Default data/model roots to \`/workspace\`, yielding the required HF checkpoint, torch-dist reference, and parquet paths.
  - Create the grader log directory, tee the foreground launcher/Ray output to \`train.log\`, and pass offline W&B mode and directory explicitly through both arguments and Ray runtime-env JSON.
  - Keep the placeholder W&B key quoted and retain the required custom generator/reward manager, \`nq_test\` test slice \`[0:3000]\`, eval interval 10, and one evaluation sample per prompt.
  - Make harmless cleanup commands non-fatal so stale-process absence cannot abort the run.
- [report.md](report.md)
  - This review and repair report.

## Expected effect

The loss-mask fix should reduce policy/KL loss contribution from retrieved observations, improve optimization stability, and increase held-out \`eval/nq_test\` exact match rather than training the model to imitate tool text. Preserving passage bodies should increase valid retrieval-supported answers and therefore raise held-out exact match and the retrieval/format reward components. The 100-rollout and logging changes ensure the grader completes the intended run and can read its fresh evaluation, rollout, truncation, optimization, and W&B evidence.
`;
const r = await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /workspace/report.md\n"+report.split("\n").map(line=>"+"+line).join("\n")+"\n*** End Patch");
text(r);
